stories.title: Stabilized a failing service
stories.situation: A fictional student service began timing out during a launch.
stories.task: Find the failure and restore a dependable path for users.
stories.action: Used logs and metrics to isolate a connection-pool bottleneck, reduced load, and documented the recovery steps.
stories.result: The service recovered and the same failure became easier to diagnose.
stories.reflection: I learned to preserve evidence before changing a stressed system.

stories.title: Removed infrastructure drift
stories.situation: A fictional lab had repeated manual configuration differences.
stories.task: Make environments reproducible without slowing small experiments.
stories.action: Captured the shared baseline as code and added a reviewable validation step.
stories.result: Rebuilds became consistent and exceptions stayed visible.
stories.reflection: Automation is most useful when its escape hatches are explicit.

stories.title: Shortened a delivery pipeline
stories.situation: A fictional project had a slow feedback loop with repeated test work.
stories.task: Reduce wait time while keeping the same quality gates.
stories.action: Separated independent checks, cached safe inputs, and measured the critical path.
stories.reflection: Speed came from removing serialization, not removing checks.

stories.title: Turned tribal knowledge into a runbook
stories.situation: A fictional team relied on one person to explain local setup.
stories.task: Make onboarding repeatable for the next contributor.
stories.action: Observed a clean setup, wrote the smallest complete runbook, and tested it with someone new.
stories.result: The next setup completed without an ad hoc handoff.
stories.reflection: Documentation should be exercised like code, not merely published.

stories.title: Made a capacity tradeoff visible
stories.situation: A fictional service had rising load and an unclear scaling threshold.
stories.task: Recommend the next change using evidence rather than intuition.
stories.action: Built a small load test, measured saturation, and compared the cost of two options.
stories.result: The team chose a bounded change with a clear follow-up trigger.
stories.reflection: A reversible decision with a measurement plan can beat a larger redesign.
